replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: These sites really do show just how deep Indigenous history in this landscape goes. That’s one of the reasons I wanted to cover Wanuskewin, the archaeological record here stretches back thousands of years, and the cultural connection to the land continues today.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: If there’s a specific fact in the video you believe is wrong, let me know which one. I tried to base the video on archaeological research and sources from Wanuskewin, the University of Saskatchewan, Parks Canada and other published material, so I’m always happy to check a specific claim.

replies.author: @freddymax5256
replies.text:
I just re-found a hammer like that in my potato patch that my Grandfather picked up in a grain field years ago.
And I have many rocks in my grain fields with lines etched into them by the disks on my farm equipment running over them for years.   
I wonder what the story about them will be when archaeologists find them hundreds of years from now?

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Honestly, that wouldn’t surprise me at all. Saskatchewan has an incredible amount of archaeological material sitting on or just below the surface. The interesting part is that the exact location and context can sometimes tell archaeologists as much as the artifact itself. I’d be curious what kinds of things the farmers around you have found.
